title: Your First HTML Page 🎉
description: Set up your workspace and create a real HTML file from scratch.

slides.title: What You Need 🛠️
slides.content:
# Your Toolkit

To start writing HTML, you only need:
- A **text editor** (like VS Code, Sublime Text, or even Notepad).
- A **web browser** (Chrome, Firefox, etc.) to view your page.
- No special server or software – HTML works right on your computer!

We recommend VS Code because it's free and has great support for web development.

slides.title: Your First HTML Snippet
slides.content: Let's write the simplest possible HTML page. Every HTML page starts with a document type declaration and basic tags.
slides.codeSnippet:
Hello, World!

This is my first web page.

quizData.question: You need an internet connection to create and view an HTML file on your own computer.
quizData.explanation: HTML files can be opened directly in a browser from your local file system – no internet needed.

slides.title: Saving & Viewing Your Page 💾
slides.content:
# Steps to Run Your First Page

1. Open your text editor (VS Code recommended).
2. Copy the code above and paste it into a new file.
3. Save the file with a `.html` extension, like `index.html`.
4. Double‑click the file to open it in your browser.
5. You should see a page with "Hello, World!" as a heading and a paragraph underneath.

**Congratulations!** You just created a website.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## File Naming

Always use **lowercase** letters and no spaces in file names. Use hyphens instead: `my-first-page.html` is better than `My First Page.html`. This avoids issues when uploading to web servers.

quizData.question: What extension must your file have to be recognised as a web page?
quizData.explanation: Web browsers look for the .html extension to render the document as HTML.
